scientific_scope_status: In the ideal equal-load one-scission interface with nu effective paths per area, peak traction=nu*f and scission work/area=nu*U_b, so their ratio is U_b/f. Required traction alone supplies no general fracture-work bound. Ideal constant-traction pullout gives work/area=sigma*ell and pays aligned fibre packing/material plus consumed sliding inventory. If each repair adds a seam that remains in series, n repairs create n(n+1)/2 independent seam-interval exposures. Explicitly unloading old seams by new deep-host connections changes that model and pays reset failures/finite anchors. A constant-damage/first-order-recovery map gives a separate steady post-load active fraction; slow biological matter replacement does not acquire that fast recovery rate.
